title: Augustana theologians: all sins mortal by nature; in regenerate some mortiferous, some not
source_text: LIV. Quod spectat Theologos Confessionis Augustanae, in eo quoque omnes con-veniunt omnia peccata esse natura sua mortalia, adeoque in irregenitis nullum esse pec-catum veniale. Verum in regenitis peccata quaedam mortalia, seu mortifera potius dici posse, quoniam eos novo mortis aeternae reatu involvunt, ac vitam in eis spiritualem extin-guunt: alia vero venialia, seu potius non mortifera, quoniam ad mortem illis non imputantur, sed propter Christum benigne condonantur. Prioris generis, juxta illos, est peccatum omne contra conscientiam, & ex malitia profectum; posterioris vero, peccata infirmitatis, pravae concupiscentiae, & similes humani lapsus. Cum hac au-tem distinctione coincidere volunt alteram illam, qua peccatum distinguitur in regnans & non regnans. Ac per peccatum mortale, sive regnans, docent renatos excutere fidem & Spiritum Sanctum, ac amittere gratiam & vitam aeternam: minime vero in haec mala incurrere per peccata quae venialia dicuntur.
pass_a_gloss: As for the theologians of the Augsburg Confession, in this also they all agree that all sins are by their nature mortal, and so in the unregenerate there is no venial sin. But in the regenerate certain sins can rather be called mortal or mortiferous, since they involve them in a new guilt of eternal death and extinguish spiritual life in them: others venial, or rather not mortiferous, since they are not imputed to them unto death but are kindly pardoned for Christ’s sake. Of the former kind, according to them, is every sin against conscience and proceeding from malice; of the latter, sins of infirmity, of depraved concupiscence, and like human falls. And with this distinction they wish that other to coincide by which sin is distinguished into reigning and not reigning. And by mortal or reigning sin they teach that the regenerate shake off faith and the Holy Spirit and lose grace and eternal life: but by no means fall into these evils through sins which are called venial.
pass_b_english: Lutheran consensus: every sin mortal by nature—none venial in the unregenerate.
In the regenerate they still mark mortiferous/reigning falls (against conscience, from malice) versus non-mortiferous infirmity slips that do not cast out Spirit and faith.
